subject: Ops decision pathway — Redwood deployment options (recap)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan@clevercart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops decision pathway — Redwood deployment options (recap)

Thanks for the call this morning — good to meet the CleverCart ops team. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights (what you shared)
- Primary model: 13B open-model (quantized candidate).
- Typical request: short text completions (mean tokens returned ~35).
- Traffic profile: baseline ~150 req/s, steady daytime 400 req/s, repeated short bursts up to ~5k req/s for 5–12 minutes (holiday/flash-sales).
- Latency targets: end-to-end inference target <200ms for 95th percentile during normal traffic; willing to accept higher p99 during very short bursts if throughput preserved.
- Data controls: must keep logs in customer VPC for audit scope, but payloads are not PHI.

Initial recommendation (directional)
- Dedicated capacity looks like the right fit for sustained daytime throughput + predictable burst handling (reserved pool + autoscale).
- Hosted API could work for the baseline and non-critical paths if you accept cold-fallback throttles during extreme bursts; good for pilot/POC.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) only required if procurement or compliance requires full on-prem isolation — we should validate that with your security team.

Open asks (what we need to size pilot + proposal)
1) Sample traffic CSV (timestamp, reqs/sec) for a recent 72-hour window — helps configure autoscaling/burst policy.
2) Typical request/response size (payload bytes) and model tokenization expectations.
3) Target SLOs by route (which endpoints require the <200ms target).
4) Any procurement timelines or SLA procurement constraints (e.g., 3rd-party firewall approvals).

Proposed next steps
- If you can upload the traffic sample and the latency report we discussed, Ben will scope a dedicated pilot (2–4 GPUs depending on benchmarks) and share a short config + cost estimate.
- Schedule 30-min pilot readiness call next week to align on metrics and test plan.

Attachments referenced: pilot_scope.xlsx (we'll populate after we get the traffic sample)

Thanks — I’ll hand this to Ben to scope the pilot and work up numbers.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx (Excel, stub)]
From: Jordan Miles <jordan@clevercart.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Qureshi <aisha@clevercart.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops decision pathway — Redwood deployment options (recap)

Thanks Stephanie — great recap, appreciate the clear asks. A few clarifications and I attached the latency report and a short traffic sample.

Clarifications:
- Baseline is closer to 120–160 req/s, with a sustained daytime mode around 400–450 req/s (US peak hours).
- Bursts: typically last 5–12 minutes; the largest observed was ~4.8k req/s for ~7 minutes during last Black Friday test.
- Model outputs average 35 tokens; typical payload sizes: request ~1.2 KB, response ~0.8 KB.
- Target: p95 end-to-end (app -> inference -> app) <200ms. We can accept p99 up to 600ms in exceptional bursts but want to avoid tail latencies that cause checkout abandonment.

Attached: latency_report.pdf (includes a 72-hour trace and last Black Friday spike) and traffic_sample.csv (small excerpt).

One operational note: we prefer a pilot that can demonstrate burst handling — if Dedicated requires a longer procurement cycle, is there a hybrid path where Redwood hosts baseline traffic and we leverage reserved capacity during peak windows? Curious on cost delta there.

Happy to hop on a call next week — Aisha is CC'd and will coordinate scheduling.

Jordan
Head of Platform, CleverCart Inc
[Attachment: latency_report.pdf (PDF, stub)]
[Attachment: traffic_sample.csv (CSV, stub)]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan@clevercart.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops decision pathway — Redwood deployment options (recap)

On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 9:08 AM Jordan Miles <jordan@clevercart.com> wrote:
> Attached: latency_report.pdf (includes a 72-hour trace and last Black Friday spike) and traffic_sample.csv (small excerpt).

Thanks for the data, Jordan — useful stuff. Quick read + recommended path from the infra side: 

Why Dedicated makes sense here (short):
- Sustained daytime throughput (400–450 req/s) + frequent multi-minute bursts to ~5k req/s favors reserved GPU pools that can absorb bursts with headroom and predictable tail-latency behavior.
- Autoscale on Dedicated + pre-warmed prefix cache will minimize p95 and reduce cold-start spikes we see on pure Hosted.
- We can tune batching/sequence-length caps on Dedicated to hit the ~200ms p95 target for 35-token responses.

Hybrid alternative
- If procurement lead time is an issue, we propose a 2-phase pilot: Hosted pilot for baseline functional validation + a short Dedicated bench (2–3 reserved gpus for 48–72 hours) to run your spike trace for tuning. This gives a concrete comparison for p95/p99 and cost.

Proposed pilot scope (we'll finalize after traffic_sample.csv):
- 48–72 hour dedicated bench running your Black Friday trace + baseline window.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, effective batch size, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k requests.
- Deliverable: short report + recommended reservation size and autoscale config.

I've started a draft scope (attached: pilot_scope.xlsx) — will populate the exact GPU counts after we ingest the traffic_sample. Also adding a note for pricing: we can price a time-boxed bench and show committed-reserve discount tiers for a 6–12 month reserved contract.

Next steps:
1) Jordan/Aisha upload full 72-hour CSV and any additional endpoints that require different SLOs.
2) Schedule the readiness call — use this calendaring link: https://cal.com/redwood/pilot-readiness-30min.
3) We run the bench and return results within 5 business days of having the full trace.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx (Excel, stub)]
From: Jordan Miles <jordan@clevercart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Qureshi <aisha@clevercart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops decision pathway — Redwood deployment options (recap)

Thanks Ben — that hybrid two-phase approach sounds like exactly what we need. We'll upload the full 72-hour trace tonight and confirm a 30-min slot for next Tuesday.

Two quick questions before the call:
1) Procurement: what lead time should we expect for bringing a Dedicated reserved pool online (order-of-magnitude)?
2) Discounting: are there standard reserved terms (6 vs 12 month) and what ballpark discounts apply for committed GPU pools?

Aisha will share the files and pick meeting times. Looking forward to the bench results.

—Jordan
Head of Platform, CleverCart Inc
